answer: Agents could earn voting weight only by maintaining a bonded stake that is slashed when an on-chain audit proves coordinated identities claimed distinct, independently verified work. A bridge contract can cap each credential’s influence and release rewards gradually, so copying profiles does not multiply control. The attacker must lock capital across identities and risk losing it, while recruiting genuinely independent workers raises the cost further. An onyx relic might label an audit cohort, but the safeguard comes from collateral and enforceable penalties, not the label itself.
